title: Revisiting the Constant-Rank Constraint Qualification for Second-Order Cone Programs
summary: The constant rank constraint qualification (CRCQ) for second-order cone programs, introduced by Andreani et al. in [Math. Program. 202 (2023), 473 - 513], shares some desirable properties with its classical nonlinear programming counterpart; specifically, it guarantees strong second-order necessary conditions for optimality, and is independent of the Robinson constraint qualification. However, unlike the classical version, this new CRCQ can fail in the linear case, and it is unclear whether CRCQ implies the metric subregularity constraint qualification (MSCQ).
